Rules / Maintainability

SK7005 The member takes more parameters than the threshold

Parameter count, including a primary constructor's parameters.

CategoryMaintainability
Default severityhint
ScopeSyntax
Needs a compilationno
Runs under --load=looseyes
Cached per fileyes
Fixno
Language version floor—
Since0.8

Why

A long parameter list is the one design smell that is unambiguous from the outside: past about seven the call sites stop being readable and start being positional puzzles, and every one of them has to change when the list does. Primary-constructor parameters count, because they are the type's constructor whatever the syntax; doc 07 § Metrics says so explicitly.

Example

Instead of:

void Configure(int a, int b, int c, int d, int e, int f, int g, int h) { }

Write:

void Configure(in ConfigureOptions options) { }

When it does not fire

A metric rule has no false positives in the sense doc 16 § R3 means: it reports a measurement against a threshold, and the measurement is either right or a bug. What it can be is useless — a threshold low enough to fire on ordinary code teaches people to switch the category off, which is the same outcome by another route. The default is therefore set well above the corpus's p99 rather than at the textbook number, and the threshold is an .editorconfig option so a repository can tighten it deliberately. Generated code is excluded from the rule entirely; doc 07 § Metrics keeps it in the aggregate numbers, which is a separate surface. A this parameter on an extension method is counted, because a caller supplies it. Generated code is excluded, which matters here: a generated record's positional constructor and a DI factory's constructor are both routinely wide and neither is a design decision anybody made.

Configuration

  • dotnet_diagnostic.SK7005.severity
  • dotnet_code_quality.SK7005.threshold (default 8)
